1.rationale: The kicker names product and category, the serif headline plus subhead frame the terms-first promise, and on both viewports the full price panel with trial terms sits inside the first screenful. What the product concretely does (photo-to-invoice) is below the fold, so comprehension of category and terms is instant but comprehension of the mechanism is deferred.

2.rationale: The pilot claim carries its full basis inline ('Internal estimate, n=11 pilot users — a small pilot, labeled as one'), the paid-by-text claim is labeled product behavior, and there is not one adjective of hype anywhere. The 'Evidence, not adjectives' section header makes the restraint itself the argument.

3.rationale: The CTA sits directly beside the complete trial terms and both prices, with the VAT note repeated in the quotation panel and the small-print section — exemplary honesty. The only flaw is there is no closing CTA: a reader who finishes the evidence section must scroll back to the top to act.

4.rationale: Price-limits-VAT-trial before any selling is exactly the IA a subscription-skeptic needs, and the quote framing ('You'd never take a job without giving one') maps the purchase decision onto the reader's own working practice. Language is plain and trade-respecting throughout, with zero startup idiom.

5.rationale: Serif display against sans body, hairline rules, left-border small-print items, and a single rust accent form a disciplined system that survives dark mode cleanly. Minor looseness: large empty space under the hero subhead on desktop and an uneven 3+2 grid in the small-print section.

6.rationale: The beta is labeled three separate times including 'Don't sign up just for it', the unverified testimonial is omitted, and the n=11 basis is set at reading size with an explicit 'not an independently verified figure'. Honesty is not just compliant here — surfacing the traps is the page's organizing principle.

7.rationale: 'The page is the quote a good tradesperson gives' is carried by the quotation panel, the small-print-set-large section, and the evidence framing — one sentence the whole page answers to. It demonstrates the transparency ethic rather than the product's actual function, a half-step short of the ideal demonstrate-the-promise form.

8.rationale: Exactly the two declared breaks are visible — pricing first and small print set large — and both live in content and typography while mechanics (feature grid, integration list, footer) stay fully conventional. I found no undeclared break in any of the four cells.

9.rationale: 'No asterisk on that line — there isn't one to hide' and 'People in Manchester, not a chat widget pretending to be' are lines no competitor could publish unchanged. The voice is fused to the quote concept and never slips into either hype or cuteness.

10.rationale: Everything needed to decide — price, caps, VAT, trial terms, CTA — is delivered in the first screenful, so the page respects the reader's time in exactly the way the product claims to. The short remainder scans in seconds with no performative devices at all.

1.rationale: The FOR row states the audience verbatim ('Sole traders who invoice from a phone between jobs'), the kicker names the category, and TERMS answers the trial question in screenful one. The headline is about the page rather than the product, so it costs one beat of cleverness before the value lands.

2.rationale: The pilot estimate is labeled with its n=11 basis and the disarming 'so we say so', the text-link claim is explained as plain product behavior, and the copy never reaches for an adjective. 'The evidence, honestly labeled' is a section title that keeps its own promise.

3.rationale: Two CTAs, both earned: one beside the TERMS row, one immediately after the 30-days-free stamp and 'walk away owing nothing' — the skeptic's objection answered at the moment of action. Prices appear only in The Total with the VAT note directly beneath them.

4.rationale: An invoice is the one document this audience reads critically every day, so line items, a total, and payment terms are natively legible IA on a phone. Price arrives after the features in conventional order, which is slightly less tuned to the subscription-skeptic than terms-first would be.

5.rationale: The document furniture is meticulous — monospace meta rows, an aligned INCLUDED column, ruled and double-ruled sections that all survive dark mode. The saturated blue CTA (periwinkle in dark) sits outside the paper-ink-green-gold palette and reads as the one imported element on an otherwise coherent sheet.

6.rationale: QuickBooks is tagged BETA with 'we won't sell it to you as finished', the unverified testimonial is gone, and the estimate is labeled as an estimate with its sample size. Nothing on the sheet rounds a signal into a fact.

7.rationale: 'The page is one worked invoice' is the ideal form the rubric names: an invoicing tool proving competence by being a competent invoice, and every section — line items, INCLUDED, total, terms, stamp — takes its orders from that single sentence. This is demonstration rather than assertion, executed edge to edge.

8.rationale: Both observed breaks match the declared block and the mechanics beneath the conceit (linear scroll, headings, standard buttons) stay conventional. The scaffold replacement reaches beyond brand-layer by definition, and the saturated blue button sits in tension with the candidate's own 'no marketing chrome anywhere' declaration.

9.rationale: 'No mental arithmetic in the merchant's car park', 'January stops being a surprise', and 'walk away owing nothing' are specific to this trade's actual Tuesdays. No competitor could lift this copy without it reading as someone else's paperwork.

10.rationale: The invoice format is inherently scannable — rows, one total, terms — and the two CTAs arrive exactly where a decision forms. The meta-conceit ('This page is an invoice') taxes the reader one beat of interpretation before the fast scan begins, which is the only friction on an otherwise time-respecting page.

1.rationale: Step one is the most concrete opening of the three — 'Job's done. Photo the job sheet' plus 'becomes a line-itemed invoice on its own' shows the product working inside the first screenful, with the kicker and trial button carrying the naming. The product identity itself is quiet (small kicker only), so recognition does the work a value statement normally would.

2.rationale: The pilot claim is labeled 'a signal, not a certified fact, and we label it as one', and step 3 carries the quiet annotation 'Product behavior, not a promise'. The section title 'What we can honestly tell you' sets the register and the copy holds it.

3.rationale: Two CTAs — top bar and directly after pricing plus trial terms — with the VAT note present at the only place prices appear, and 'no card required' stated verbatim. 'Try the whole afternoon on us' adds a small flourish to an otherwise clean, unnagging path.

4.rationale: Six numbered steps read like a trade method statement and stack perfectly on a phone, and 'the ladder's still warm' is genuine trade language. Price sits at the very bottom in conventional price-last order, and 'Plays well with your bank' is a borrowed SaaS-ism — two small misfits for a subscription skeptic.

5.rationale: Display numerals, bold step heads, body text, and small-caps labels make a clean, consistent hierarchy with disciplined rules between steps in both modes. The gold/green split on the numerals (green for 3 and 6 only) has a decodable money-logic but reads as semi-arbitrary at first pass — step 5 is also money and stays gold.

6.rationale: Beta is tagged and glossed 'we won't pretend it's done', the unverified testimonial is omitted, and the n=11 estimate is fully labeled. The 'not a promise' annotation on step 3 shows honesty applied even where the data is verified.

7.rationale: 'Six plain steps from job done to money put aside' is a real signature that content, numerals, and even the tax-pot closing line ('job done, money in, tax sorted') all reinforce. It narrates recognition of the reader's afternoon rather than demonstrating the artifact itself, which keeps it a notch below the demonstrate-the-promise ideal.

8.rationale: Exactly the two declared breaks appear — story-step opening and display numerals as the graphic language — both brand-layer, while every mechanic (top bar, integration list, pricing table, footer) stays conventional. The second accent ink on the numerals is a palette choice inside the declared break, not an undeclared one.

9.rationale: 'The paperwork is finished while the ladder's still warm' and 'you stay the reasonable one without writing a word' are distinctive and trade-true. 'Try the whole afternoon on us' and 'plays well with' drift toward generic marketing warmth, which a competitor could publish unchanged.

10.rationale: The six steps scan in seconds, the numerals index the page like a job sheet, and nothing on it is performative. The skeptic's price question is answered only at the bottom of the story, so the page is fast to scan but slightly slower to decide than its own promise implies.
